title: Stochastic seqlen-mixture throughput portrait for multi-GPU TP/PP inference
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: build a repeatable benchmarking harness that profiles steady-state and burst throughput for multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) inference under stochastic sequence-length mixtures. The goal is a ‘throughput portrait’ that captures tokens/sec, p95 latency, p99 tails, and variance across realistic seqlen distributions (conversational short, doc medium, long-context), and to surface regressions automatically. This is aimed at surfacing regression classes missed by uniform-length soak tests: seqlen friction, KV-cache churn, attention-kernel switching, and stage imbalance in TP/PP combos.

Approach: (1) Define canonical seqlen mixtures from production traces and synthetic tails. (2) Implement tokenstorm generator that replays seqlen mixes with realistic prefix reuse and KV cache hit patterns. (3) Run matrix across representative mesh sizes (e.g., 8xV100-like, 16xA10, 4xH100-pp-heavy) for TP/PP variants. (4) Capture per-stage throughput, inter-GPU NVLink utilization, CPU-to-GPU enqueue latencies, and memory growth profiles. (5) Add automated regression detection using baseline fingerprinting (median + rolling MAD) and alerting on >3 sigma drift and p95 slippage >15%.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run non-blocking for 4 hours at target load with stable KV-cache reuse patterns
Portrait output includes tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, per-stage utilization, NVLink bandwidth heatmap, and seqlen bucket breakdown
Automated regression detector produces reproducible alerts on injected performance regressions (we inject synthetic stage imbalance and kernel slowdown for validation)
Results reproducible across runs within 8% tokens/sec variance for the same seed and profile
Benchmark results are stored to the throughput insights dashboard and a CSV/Parquet artifact is uploaded for downstream analysis
steps: Curate seqlen mixtures: extract 3 weeks of convo and document traces, bucket into short/medium/long profiles and synthesize heavy-tail examples
Implement tokenstorm workload generator with configurable prefix reuse and KV cache hit probability
Add hooks in runtime to emit per-stage metrics and attach lightweight labels for TP/PP mapping
Run hardware matrix overnight on staging cluster, collect artifacts to GCS and the throughput dashboard
Validate regression detector by replaying baseline and then replaying runs with deliberate slowdowns (kernel sleep or stage skew)
Consolidate findings, write one-pager with recommendations (warmup changes, batching policy, kernel selection heuristics) and add follow-up ENG tickets
hardware_matrix: 16x mixed A100/H100 (heterogeneous) — stress and imbalance case
8x V100 (legacy) — regression guardrail for older customers
synthetic_profiles: ConvShort (70% <64 tokens, 25% 64-512, 5% >512) — high QPS low seqlen
DocMix (40% <128, 40% 128-1024, 20% >1024) — mixed load with longer tails
LongTail (20% <256, 30% 256-2k, 50% >2k) — heavy KV churn + memory pressure
BurstStorm (bursty arrival with 10x transient load for 30s every 10m) — microburst sensitivity
metrics_tracked: KV-cache hit rate and cache churn
alerting_thresholds: p95 increase > 15% vs baseline for 3 consecutive runs -> file regression alert
global tokens/sec drop > 10% with CPU/NVLink utilization unchanged -> investigate kernel or serialization regression
KV-cache hit-rate drop > 8% correlated with p95 tail increase
per-stage tokens/sec imbalance > 20% (indicates stage skew in PP)
deliverables: Benchmark harness merged to repo under infra/bench/tokenstorm
Canonical seqlen mixture definitions (YAML) committed to repo
Dashboard panel in Throughput Insights with historical portraits
One-pager with recommended runtime configuration changes and follow-up ENG tickets
Regression detector jobs scheduled nightly with PR integration gate
